subject.title: Preserve structured ACP backend error kinds instead of mapping all errors to `end_turn`

question: Should non-refusal Gateway chat failures in the ACP bridge reject `session/prompt` with structured `RequestError`s, or should they continue resolving `PromptResponse` while exposing structured failure data through another approved surface?
rationale: Current ACP stop reasons cannot directly express timeout, rate-limit, or server-error classes, and changing prompt settlement from resolved responses to JSON-RPC rejection is a client-visible compatibility choice.

options.title: Approve RequestError Settlement After Fixes
options.body: Use rejected prompt responses for backend failures, but require non-conflicting error codes/data, intentional reconnect behavior, tests, and real ACP proof before merge.

options.title: Preserve Resolved Prompt Responses
options.body: Keep existing prompt resolution as the default and expose structured backend failure data through an explicitly approved metadata or diagnostic surface.

options.title: Pause For Maintainer Replacement
options.body: Keep the issue open and ask for a narrower maintainer-led implementation if the current branch cannot settle the compatibility contract and proof gap.

recommendation.title: Approve RequestError Settlement After Fixes
recommendation.body: Use rejected prompt responses for backend failures, but require non-conflicting error codes/data, intentional reconnect behavior, tests, and real ACP proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The recent structured error-kind implementation and tests trace through this owner signal, making it the best available routing point for the ACP contract decision.
